findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC requiring the pre-push live gate result (50 direct calls per (variant, prompt) cell with 0 filtered; 5 runner calls per cell with 0 filtered and all parsed) to be recorded in a ticket comment before the Gerrit push.
evidence: Testing: "Live, before push (recorded in a ticket comment): direct converse, 50 calls per (variant, prompt) cell, pass = 0 filtered; through the rebar runner, 5 per cell, pass = 0 filtered and every reply parses."
The first AC covers root-cause evidence only. The live AC is one Live External Integration run. No AC references the 50/5-per-cell gate.
findings.finding: The pre-push live validation gate described under Testing has no covering acceptance criterion. That gate is 50 direct converse calls per (variant, prompt) cell with 0 filtered, plus 5 runner calls per cell with 0 filtered and every reply parsing, recorded in a ticket comment. The only live AC is a single CI run, which does not show robustness at the 50-sample level.
findings.location: Testing (Live, before push) vs Acceptance criteria
scenarios: An executor pushes after one green dispatch run without running the 50-call gate. The fix is flaky (e.g. 1 in 20 filtered), so the scheduled Sunday run fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: "[non-codebase] Before push, a ticket comment records per-(variant, prompt) cell counts: direct converse 50/50 not filtered; rebar runner 5/5 not filtered and parsed as CompletionVerdict."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Measure the real `completion-verifier` prompt on Opus/Sonnet 5.5 with a met AC plus satisfying evidence for parse/validation success (not just filtering), and record it; if it fails, file a runtime follow-up instead of relying on the test-only "empty when met" clause.
evidence: "without it Opus 5.5 returned per-criterion findings lacking `detail`, which fail `CompletionVerdict` validation (0/20 parsed); with it 10/10 per variant parsed"
"The empty-evidence production path is therefore not filtered at these sample sizes ... No runtime change is in scope." — the measurement reports filter counts only, not parse counts
Production measurement cases were 'AC but no evidence' and 'neither'; there is no case with an AC plus satisfying evidence, which is the case that produced the parse failures.
findings.finding: The plan discovered a second Opus 5.5 behaviour beyond the filter, and production may share it unmeasured. When the evidence shows the criterion met, Opus 5.5 returned per-criterion findings lacking `detail`, which fail `CompletionVerdict` validation (0/20 parsed). The plan fixes this only in the test prompt, with the clause "empty when every criterion is met". Its production-exposure measurement covered only content_filtered, not parse/validation success of the real `completion-verifier` prompt against a met criterion. So the scoping "No runtime change is in scope" is not grounded for this second behaviour. Tuning the test prompt to parse may mask a production regression the matrix exists to detect.
findings.location: Approach — "The 'empty when met' clause is needed" / Root cause — "Production exposure, measured"
scenarios: A production completion-verifier run on Opus or Sonnet 5.5 with a met criterion and real evidence returns findings without `detail`, `CompletionVerdict` validation fails, and the verify step errors. Meanwhile the matrix test stays green because its prompt now carries a clause production lacks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the pre-push live runs (direct converse 50/cell and runner 5/cell) cover every model id the `external LLM (live bedrock)` job calls from `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`, and record per-model counts in the ticket comment.
evidence: "06b3b1a5230 (Gerrit 3340), which moved `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` to the 5.5 ids"
"direct converse, 50 calls per (variant, prompt) cell, pass = 0 filtered" — no model id stated
Root cause: "Measured live on Bedrock Opus 5.5"; the fix text was measured 10/10 "per variant" on Opus only
findings.finding: The live pre-push validation does not name which model ids it runs against. The triggering commit moved `bedrock.toml` to "the 5.5 ids" (plural), but the root-cause and fix measurements name only Opus 5.5. The Testing section says "50 calls per (variant, prompt) cell" without stating which model(s). The new prompt and the "empty when met" clause could be filtered or fail parsing on another 5.5 id the matrix runs, which would only surface at the post-merge CI run.
scenarios: The matrix also exercises another 5.5 id from bedrock.toml (e.g. Sonnet 5.5). The new prompt passes pre-push on Opus, then the CI arm fails on the other id, and the scheduled Sunday run misses its target.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Testing bullet to: "direct converse, 50 calls per (model id in bedrock.toml × variant × prompt) cell ...; through the rebar runner, 5 per such cell ...".

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Implement the 'exactly one JSON object before "emit your FINAL"' edge test with the existing `sm._object_spans` (or `_all_json_objects`) rather than a new regex or brace counter.
evidence: tests/external/_structured_matrix.py:15-21 already imports `_all_json_objects` from `rebar.llm.structured`.
tests/external/_structured_matrix.py:48 `_object_spans(text)` returns '(start, end_inclusive, value)' for every top-level parseable object — exactly the count and position this test needs.
Plan text names the assertion but not the mechanism.
findings.finding: The edge test 'the agentic prompt contains exactly one JSON object, placed before "emit your FINAL"' does not say how JSON objects are counted. That leaves room for a hand-rolled regex or brace counter in the unit test, which would duplicate the string-aware brace scanner already used by the harness's own scorer.
findings.location: Testing — 'Unit, edge: … the agentic prompt contains exactly one JSON object, placed before "emit your FINAL"'
scenarios: A test author writes `re.findall(r'\{.*?\}', AGENTIC_TRANSCRIPT_PROMPT)`. This miscounts if a later prompt edit adds a nested or brace-bearing string, and it drifts from how the scorer itself sees objects.
findings.suggested_fix: In the edge test: `spans = sm._object_spans(prompt); assert len(spans) == 1; start, end, value = spans[0]; assert end < prompt.index("emit your FINAL"); assert value["target_id"] != "7c41-0d2e-9a85-b613"` (the verified ticket id typed as a literal in the test, per the plan's literal-pinning rule).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the 'empty when met' A/B parse counts to the ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE comment (or a follow-up comment): with and without the clause, parsed/total per (variant, prompt) cell through the runner. Make the plan's sample sizes match the comment's.
evidence: Plan: 'without it Opus 5.5 returned per-criterion findings lacking `detail`, which fail `CompletionVerdict` validation (0/20 parsed); with it 10/10 per variant parsed.'

ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE comment (show_ticket mustard-fungoid-grackle) ends with: 'Replacement prompts ... direct converse: 0/50 in each of the 4 (variant, prompt) cells = 0/200; through the runner 0/20 per variant.' It gives no parse counts and no A/B on the 'empty when met' clause.
Plan: 'Shipped text (exactly what was measured)'. The measured record for the wording choice that matters most is missing.
findings.finding: The plan says the full counts are in the ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE comment. But the measurement behind the 'empty when met' wording is not there. The comment does not contain 'without it ... 0/20 parsed; with it 10/10 per variant parsed'. Its only runner figure is 'through the runner 0/20 per variant', which counts filtered replies and gives no parse count. The sample sizes also disagree: 10 per variant in the plan, 20 in the comment.
findings.location: Approach — paragraph starting 'The "empty when met" clause is needed'; Root cause — 'full counts in the ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE comment on this ticket'
scenarios: A reviewer or a later maintainer wants to drop the 'empty when met' clause. The ticket has no recorded parse A/B, so the plan's statement that the clause is needed cannot be checked.
The runner check before push ('5 per cell ... every reply parses') is checked against a baseline that was never written down.
findings.suggested_fix: Post a ticket comment with the runner counts for both wordings, e.g. 'without empty-when-met: parsed 0/20 (findings missing detail); with: parsed N/N per variant'. Then change the plan's '10/10 per variant' to the recorded figure, or change the comment's '0/20 per variant' so they agree.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either justify why the 0/200 sample is enough for 40 CI draws per run, or also have the harness record `LLMInputRejectedError` as a counted `filtered` outcome (test-only) with an explicit threshold assertion instead of aborting on the first filtered reply.
evidence: test_structured_output_matrix.py:188 asserts only `all_scores` (parse failures are counted, not fatal), while any exception from `runner.run(req)` at line 115 aborts the sweep
Plan Testing: 'direct converse, 50 calls per (variant, prompt) cell, pass = 0 filtered; through the rebar runner, 5 per cell'
CI makes 2 variants × 2 prompts × _N_REPEATS=10 = 40 Opus calls for the bedrock cell (bedrock.toml `model = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`)
Ticket goal: 'needs the scheduled run (Sunday 2026-11-15 ~22:16 PST) green'
findings.finding: The fix relies only on lowering a stochastic per-call filter rate. The harness itself stays fail-fast: one `content_filtered` reply anywhere in the ~40 Opus calls of a run raises out of `_live_reply` and fails the job, even though the harness already treats parse failures as data (it asserts only `all_scores`). The pre-push gate (0 filtered in 50 direct calls per cell, 5 per cell through the runner) only bounds the per-call rate to about ≤1.5% at 95% confidence, which still leaves a real chance of a filtered call across 40 CI draws on the single scheduled run the ticket depends on. A simpler, more robust test-only option the plan doesn't consider: catch `LLMInputRejectedError` in `_live_reply`, record it as a measured `filtered` outcome in `score_table.json`, and assert a threshold. That keeps 'no runtime change' and makes the filter rate visible instead of fatal.
scenarios: A rare residual filter (e.g. 1 in 100) on the Sunday run fails the job again even though the new prompt is mostly fine
A future Bedrock model bump changes filter sensitivity, and the harness fails with no measurement artifact instead of reporting a filter rate

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the verdict request, give the `findings` item shape (each item needs `criterion` and `detail`), or state that findings must be empty for PASS. Add a unit assertion for it.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:78-82: `VerdictFinding.criterion: str = Field(...)` and `detail: str = Field(...)` are required with no default.
Plan: "without it Opus 5.5 returned per-criterion findings lacking `detail`, which fail `CompletionVerdict` validation (0/20 parsed)".
Plan's request text: "a `findings` array (empty when every criterion is met)". No item fields are named.
findings.finding: The verdict request names the `findings` array but never gives the shape of a finding item. `CompletionVerdict.findings` items (`VerdictFinding`) require `criterion` and `detail`. The plan's own measurement found that a reply with findings but no `detail` fails validation 0/20. The plan only avoids that path by hoping findings stay empty ('empty when every criterion is met'). Any reply that returns FAIL, or adds a non-empty finding, still has no defined item vocabulary.
findings.location: Approach — verdict request text; tests/external/_structured_matrix.py SINGLE_SHOT_PROMPT / AGENTIC_TRANSCRIPT_PROMPT
scenarios: A non-Opus cell (anthropic/openai overlays) or a future model upgrade adds a per-criterion finding on a PASS, or returns FAIL. The reply then fails to parse and the 'every reply parses' gate breaks again.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the shared request to: '…a `findings` array (empty when every criterion is met; otherwise one object per failing criterion with `criterion` and `detail` strings), and a `summary` string.' Re-measure live before shipping, since this changes the text.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the harness handles a filtered or failed live call: either record it as a counted `filtered` reply or artifact and keep sweeping, or deliberately keep fail-fast. If fail-fast, give the residual per-run failure probability the 0/50 evidence supports.
evidence: tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py:101-116: `_live_reply` calls `runner.run(req)` with no exception handling.
Searching tests/external for 'LLMInputRejectedError' finds no matches, so no handler exists.
test_structured_output_matrix.py:69 `_N_REPEATS = 10`, and the loop at :154-159 makes 40 calls per cell.
Plan Testing: "50 calls per (variant, prompt) cell, pass = 0 filtered". It says nothing about what the harness does if a filter happens in CI.
findings.finding: The plan gives no fallback for a call that still comes back `content_filtered` (or fails some other way) during the CI sweep. `_live_reply` lets `LLMInputRejectedError` propagate, so one filtered call out of the 40 per Bedrock cell (2 variants × 2 prompts × `_N_REPEATS=10`) fails the whole job. The plan's pre-push evidence (0/50 per cell) still allows a per-call filter rate of up to about 6% at 95% confidence, which does not guarantee the scheduled run the AC depends on stays green.
findings.location: Approach / Scope — tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py `_live_reply` and sweep loop; AC 'external LLM (live bedrock) concluding success'
scenarios: The Sunday scheduled run hits one filtered reply out of 40. The job fails with the same symptom and ticket unkempt-amaranth-archerfish misses its green-run requirement.
A transient provider-side refusal on one repeat discards the whole cell's measurement instead of being recorded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Inline the exact measured literals (shared block, agentic role line, verdict request) in a fenced code block or cite the ticket comment containing them verbatim, and state that PROMPTS is a sequence of (label, prompt) pairs (or a dict).
evidence: "shared block: `Ticket 7c41-0d2e-9a85-b613 has one acceptance criterion: "`add(a, b)` returns the sum of its arguments." ...`" (nested backticks)
"both requests read: a JSON object with `verdict` (PASS or FAIL), a `findings` array (empty when every criterion is met), and a `summary` string." (paraphrase, not a literal)
"`PROMPTS`" has no stated type.
findings.finding:
The plan says the shipped text is 'exactly what was measured', but the exact literals cannot be recovered from the plan.
- The shared block nests inline-code backticks inside a backtick span. It is therefore ambiguous whether the string itself contains backticks around `add(a, b)`, the test node id, `src/calc.py` and `def add...`.
- The verdict request is only paraphrased ('both requests read: a JSON object with ...').
- The PROMPTS container shape (dict vs sequence of (label, prompt) pairs) is unstated.
Because a one-token change can alter filter behaviour, the executor must either guess or go back to the ticket comment.
scenarios: The executor drops or adds backticks, or rewords the verdict request. The shipped prompt then differs from the measured one and the measured 0-filtered result no longer applies.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the inline-code shared block and the paraphrased request with a fenced code block of the exact Python string literals. Add: "PROMPTS: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ((\"agentic_transcript\", AGENTIC_TRANSCRIPT_PROMPT), (\"single_shot\", SINGLE_SHOT_PROMPT))" or whichever shape the existing parametrization uses.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Write out the full verbatim `AGENTIC_TRANSCRIPT_PROMPT` and `SINGLE_SHOT_PROMPT` strings exactly as measured (including whether the 'emit your FINAL CompletionVerdict' lead-in and the 'return PASS' tail are kept) so the shipped text is unambiguous.
evidence: Plan: 'agentic: the existing role line, the shared block, the existing quoted … record, then the verdict request.'
Plan: 'both requests read: a JSON object with `verdict` (PASS or FAIL), a `findings` array (empty when every criterion is met), and a `summary` string.'
Current test_structured_output_matrix.py:46-48 and 52-54 contain the lead-ins and 'return PASS' tails, and the plan doesn't say what happens to them
Plan Testing edge: JSON object 'placed before "emit your FINAL"'
findings.finding: The plan says the shipped text is 'exactly what was measured' and the filter is shown to be wording-sensitive (removing the system prompt flips 8/8 to 0/8). Yet only the shared block is given verbatim. The verdict request is paraphrased ('both requests read: a JSON object with `verdict` (PASS or FAIL), a `findings` array (empty when every criterion is met), and a `summary` string'). It is also unclear whether the existing lead-ins and tails ('Having read it, emit your FINAL CompletionVerdict for the ticket:', 'Return a CompletionVerdict for…', 'The acceptance criteria are met, so return PASS.' / 'Return PASS.') are kept, changed, or dropped. The edge test even depends on the phrase 'emit your FINAL', which the plan never states is retained. An implementer rebuilding from this paraphrase can ship a string that was never measured, which undermines the plan's own guarantee.
findings.location: Approach — 'Shipped text (exactly what was measured)' bullets
scenarios: The implementer drops 'The acceptance criteria are met, so return PASS.' (or keeps it where the measured version didn't), producing an unmeasured prompt that may filter or parse differently

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Write out the full literal text of AGENTIC_TRANSCRIPT_PROMPT and SINGLE_SHOT_PROMPT (including the dependency-record lead-in, the 'emit your FINAL CompletionVerdict' lead-in, and whether 'Return PASS.'/'…so return PASS.' stay), exactly as measured.
evidence: Plan: "agentic: the existing role line, the shared block, the existing quoted … record, then the verdict request."
Plan: "both requests read: a JSON object with `verdict` (PASS or FAIL), a `findings` array (empty when every criterion is met), and a `summary` string." This is a paraphrase, not a literal.

Current text at tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py:44-48 and :52-54 includes 'A dependency-lookup tool returned this record verbatim:', 'Having read it, emit your FINAL CompletionVerdict…', 'The acceptance criteria are met, so return PASS.' and 'Return PASS.'. The plan doesn't say what happens to any of them.
Plan unit edge test: "placed before \"emit your FINAL\"". This assumes a lead-in the shipped text never spells out.
findings.finding: The plan says the shipped text is 'exactly what was measured', but it only paraphrases the verdict-request sentence and the agentic glue lines. It doesn't say whether the existing lead-in 'A dependency-lookup tool returned this record verbatim:', the 'Having read it, emit your FINAL CompletionVerdict for the ticket:' lead-in (the edge test needs 'emit your FINAL' to exist), or the PASS-steering sentences ('The acceptance criteria are met, so return PASS.' / 'Return PASS.') are kept, changed or dropped. These are exactly the request features the plan showed the content filter and the parse rate depend on.
findings.location: Approach — 'Shipped text (exactly what was measured)' / 'both requests read: …'
scenarios: The implementer drops 'Return PASS.' or rewords the lead-in, which changes the request the filter and parser measurements were taken on.
The unit test's hand-written literals and the module constants both follow the implementer's reading, so the pin passes while the text no longer matches the ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE measurement.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either change 'pins the whole request' to 'pins the system prompt and base prompts', or also move `_apply_variant` into `_structured_matrix.py` and add a unit test that pins the sentinel-variant request.
evidence: tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py:66 `_SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE = "\n\n" + structured.SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE` and :72-77 `_apply_variant` stay in the external module; the plan's Scope moves only SYSTEM_PROMPT / AGENTIC_TRANSCRIPT_PROMPT / SINGLE_SHOT_PROMPT / PROMPTS.
tests/unit/test_structured_matrix_scorer.py imports only `_structured_matrix as sm` (line 23), not the external test module, which it deliberately does not collect (docstring lines 5-6).
Testing section: the unit assertions cover the prompt contents, labels, SYSTEM_PROMPT, '{' absence and JSON-object placement. None covers the sentinel-appended request.
findings.finding: The plan says moving the prompts lets the offline oracle 'pin the whole request'. It does not. The sentinel variant changes the request by appending a directive in `_apply_variant` / `_SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE`, and the plan leaves both in `tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py`. The unit oracle cannot import that module, and the planned tests check only the base prompts and `SYSTEM_PROMPT`. Half the measured cells, the sentinel/* ones, are sent with text the oracle never sees.
findings.location: Approach — 'so the offline oracle `tests/unit/test_structured_matrix_scorer.py` pins the whole request'; Scope — `tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py`
scenarios: Someone edits `structured.SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE` or `_apply_variant` so that a sentinel/* cell gets filtered again. The offline oracle stays green and the failure shows up only in the live bedrock job.
